clue.text: Characteristic of Father Brown, wandering once into local church

indicators.note: into says the scrambled word is placed inside the pub-and-church pair

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so the word once is rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on the priest-detective, who once roamed into a nearby church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns ONCE into OCEN, which goes 'into' INN + CE. 'Local' is British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Chesterton's first collection is titled after the priest-detective's guilelessness, his defining quality.

clue.text: Provide with cover against current disaster

definitions.text: Provide with cover against current disaster

parts.words: Provide with cover against current disaster
parts.note: read as wrapping electrical wiring so the flow of electricity cannot cause harm, not as an insurance policy for a present catastrophe

explanation.surface: An insurer offers a policy for a disaster happening now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' and 'current' suggest insurance and present events; really it is a plastic sheath on a wire carrying electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping a conductor in non-conducting material shields people and things from electric shock or fire.

clue.text: Material don got from two cities where Times is published

indicators.note: got from says the word don is extracted from the pair of city names

parts.words: two cities where Times is published
parts.note: the New York Times and The Times of London: NY plus LONDON
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university lecturer acquires a fabric from two newspaper cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don' looks like a lecturer but is just the letters DON, taken out of NY + LONDON.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a synthetic fibre woven into fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Janitor who heeds a common parting exhortation?

definitions.text: who heeds a common parting exhortation?
definitions.meaning: people say 'take care' when parting; one who obeys takes care

explanation.surface: A school janitor listens when people say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building; split up, the word describes someone taking care as urged.

clue.text: Oriental males upset over little sibling's fate

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word for males reads upward

parts.note: men are males
E is short for East, Oriental
sis is a short, familiar word for sister

explanation.surface: Eastern men are distressed about their small sister's destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MEN into NEM; 'over' just puts that above E + SIS in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Nemesis was the goddess of retribution, so the word means one's downfall or doom.

clue.text: Language briefly identified by head of Eton

definitions.text: Language briefly identified by head of Eton

parts.words: Language briefly identified by head of Eton
parts.note: the single letter E, first of Eton, is the standard short form for the language of England

explanation.surface: An Eton headmaster quickly recognises a language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of Eton' is not the headmaster but its first letter, E, the dictionary abbreviation for this tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in England is abbreviated E in dictionaries.

clue.text: Faint-hearted booby in retreat out West

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the shortened word is read from the end
out says the letter for West is removed

parts.note: a booby is a fool, a dimwit

explanation.surface: A cowardly fool runs away in the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes W from DIMWIT to leave DIMIT, which 'in retreat' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint-hearted and lacking courage are synonyms of shy and fearful.

clue.text: He's put out by the requests for jobs

indicators.note: put out says the letters of He's pronoun are removed

parts.note: asks are requests
the pronoun he

explanation.surface: A man is annoyed by what people keep asking him to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed, but it removes HE from THE ASKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks and jobs are synonyms for pieces of work to be done.

clue.text: Inclination to enter wet area in Moroccan city

indicators.note: to enter says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a marsh is boggy land
rake is a slope or angle, as of a stage

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to step into a swampy part of a North African city.
explanation.walkthrough: RAKE, a theatrical stage's slope, goes 'to enter' MARSH.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a major city in Morocco, at the foot of the Atlas mountains.

clue.text: Daughter's taken on one instrument, with low concentration

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
I is the Roman numeral one
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A daughter takes up an instrument but can't concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with low concentration' is the chemist's sense of watered down, not an inattentive player.
explanation.definitionFit: A weakened solution has had water added, so its concentration is low.

clue.text: Like a certain star, become a high-flier about 50

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, one word around the numeral

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
L is the Roman numeral 50

explanation.surface: Someone becomes a star, rising high at around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: SOAR goes 'about' L, the Roman 50.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertaining to the sun, our own star.

clue.text: A last grim representation of a master

indicators.note: a representation re-presents something in new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A final, bleak portrait of an old master painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges A LAST GRIM; 'of' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin magister, teacher, it means characteristic of or befitting a master.

clue.text: Medicine produced by day in eastern county

indicators.note: in says the day abbreviation goes inside the county

parts.note: LINCS is Lincolnshire, an English county on the east coast
TU is short for Tuesday

explanation.surface: A remedy manufactured one day in the east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincolnshire is an English county on the North Sea coast, abbreviated LINCS; TU (Tuesday) goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A syrupy cough mixture, a kind of medicine.

clue.text: Shake requiring little preparation

definitions.meaning: a moment, as in 'in two shakes'
ready at once, as soluble coffee is

explanation.surface: A quick milkshake mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a moment of time and food that is ready immediately.

clue.text: Very friendly but stupid, like those with taking ways?

parts.note: thick is British slang for stupid
as means like
thieves take things, a pun on 'taking ways' meaning charming manners

explanation.surface: Pally but dim, like charming people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ways' usually means charm; here it means stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two people very close and conspiratorial.

clue.text: Without stopping to think, I put mouse out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Acting rashly, someone puts the pet mouse outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I PUT MOUSE; the OCR dropped the I that the scan shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting rashly and on impulse means doing so without reflection.

clue.text: Former City mob, half-heartedly offensive

parts.note: ex means former
EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: half-heartedly removes half of the pair of letters at the word's centre

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly mob

explanation.surface: A one-time crowd from the City behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the City of London's postcode; 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two middle Bs of RABBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Execrable means abominable, extremely bad or offensive.

clue.text: East or West, as against North or South

definitions.text: East or West, as against North or South

parts.words: East or West, as against North or South
parts.note: in bridge, the East-West pair play against the North-South pair

explanation.surface: Looks like geography or politics, comparing compass directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points are bridge seats: the partnerships East-West and North-South face each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Each player is a rival of the pair across the table in the card game.

clue.text: Period of probation one is bound to serve

definitions.text: Period of probation one is bound to serve

parts.words: Period of probation one is bound to serve
parts.note: a trainee is bound by indentures to a master for a term of learning, not a convict serving a sentence

explanation.surface: Sounds like a criminal on probation who must serve a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probation' and 'serve' suggest a court sentence; 'bound' is the indentured trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade learner was legally bound to work for a master for a fixed trial term.

clue.text: Character on staff — one certain to succeed

definitions.meaning: a musical sign on the stave cancelling a sharp or flat
a person born with the gift, a sure thing

explanation.surface: An employee with personality is bound to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a musical symbol and a person with innate talent.

clue.text: Member of group selected for team run

parts.note: picked for the team means in the side
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A club member is picked for the team and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: IN SIDE means picked for the team; R is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone within an organisation, with inside knowledge.

clue.text: Parking in splendid setting for a meal

indicators.note: a setting holds a jewel, so the adjective encloses the parking letter

parts.note: super means splendid
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: A car park in a lovely location for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SUPER is the 'setting' for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal.

clue.text: Appearing for trial, drunk and showing irritation

parts.note: to be up before the court is to stand trial
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A defendant turns up to court drunk and cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' before the magistrates is British for appearing in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and irritable, unable to relax.

clue.text: Fish very quietly consumed by cat

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten, held within the other word

parts.note: cat is jazz slang for a man, a guy
PP is pianissimo, very quiet in music

explanation.surface: A fish silently eaten by a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' suggests a feline eating a fish, but in jazz slang a cat is simply a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: A blow experienced in Africa by knighted commanders

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
OC, officer commanding
CO, commanding officer

explanation.surface: Knighted generals take a blow in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' is a wind, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot, dusty wind blowing from North Africa.

clue.text: South American mammal — caught one eating grass

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the pair surrounds the grass word

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral one
the oat is a cereal grass

explanation.surface: An animal is caught eating grass.
explanation.walkthrough: C + I go round OAT ('eating').
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon-like animal of Central and South America.

clue.text: Made a fortune from Merimee edition

parts.note: Prosper Merimee, the French author of Carmen

explanation.surface: Someone got rich from an edition of the French novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Merimee's first name is Prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow rich is to thrive financially.

clue.text: A couple that may turn a bit boring?

definitions.meaning: a pair, as of game birds

definitions.text: that may turn a bit boring?
definitions.meaning: a hand drill turned by a crank, holding a bit for boring holes

explanation.surface: A pair who could make something a little dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a pair and a carpenter's tool that rotates a drill bit.

clue.text: Dodgy when female leaves in high spirits

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter for female is taken away

parts.note: frisky means in high spirits

explanation.surface: Things get dicey when a woman walks out of a lively party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high spirits' stands for being lively, FRISKY; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy is British slang for hazardous or uncertain.

clue.text: Old criminal arrayed in scarlet

indicators.note: arrayed means dressed or set out anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A felon of old dressed in red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrayed' rearranges IN SCARLET. Larceny ceased to be a crime in England in 1968, hence 'Old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief, guilty of the former crime of theft of goods.
